paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. God gave this promise to a man locked in a courtyard, with an army outside the walls and a city about to fall. Even then, the LORD says, "Call to Me, and I will answer…" (Jeremiah 33:3). Your worst day is not too small or too messy for Him to hear.

Now listen to the turn. God does not pretend the wickedness wasn't there, and He says so plainly (Jeremiah 33:5). But then comes that one word, "Nevertheless," and He promises "health and healing" (Jeremiah 33:6). He says He will cleanse them "from all the iniquity they have committed against Me," and "forgive all their sins of rebellion against Me" (Jeremiah 33:8). I spent years in the back of a drawer, so I know what it is to think the story is over, and God is the One who writes the nevertheless.

And He doesn't leave it as a feeling. He promises a righteous Branch for David (Jeremiah 33:15), and He ties His promise to the day and the night, which still show up on time (Jeremiah 33:20). So when the world says God has given up on His people, you can look at the sunrise and say, "Not today, and not ever." The days are coming, and that's why I keep my ovens ready, so keep your heart ready too. This teaching isn't over, friend.
